title: Optimization of Nutritional Care in Inpatients After Oncological Surgery
summary:
The aim of this study is to evaluate the effectiveness and feasibility of a high-protein, high-calorie diet for patients who are hospitalized after cancer surgery involving the digestive tract. The study will investigate whether this type of diet helps patients meet their energy and protein requirements better than the standard hospital diet.

In addition, the study will explore whether the nutritional intervention may have beneficial effects on patients' nutritional status, body composition, muscle strength, recovery after surgery, length of hospital stay, and quality of life. The findings will help determine whether a high-protein, high-calorie diet can be successfully implemented in routine clinical care and contribute to improved postoperative recovery.

interventions.name: Patients with colorectal or pankreatic cancer will be served standard hospital food post tumor surgery.
Patients with colorectal or pankreatic cancer will be served food enriched in proteins of 1,5g protein per body weight and increased calories (30kcal/kg body weight) post tumor surgery.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
The study population will consist of patients diagnosed with pancreatic cancer (ICD-10 C25) or colorectal cancer (ICD-10 C18, C19, C20) who are scheduled to undergo oncological visceral surgical procedures.
Exclusion criteria:
Patients will be excluded if they are younger than 18 years of age, are pregnant or breastfeeding, follow a vegetarian or vegan diet, or are unable to provide informed consent.
